title: I Took the Scholarship Essay Prompt Back to the Donor

parts.text: I read the winning essay and heard my student's story with the serial numbers filed off. I am forty-one, teacher, ceremony folding chair hurting. The winner, a board kid named Paige, had written about 'my cafeteria job.' My student, Luis, has the cafeteria job. Paige does not. Luis had shown me his draft in office hours, specific: spilled ranch on a name tag. Paige's essay had the ranch. Paige said, "It's just inspiration" I said, "It's his ranch" The gym smelled like floor wax and corsages. I can still name the ugly little detail, which is how I know it happened. I noticed a scuff on the floor shaped like a comma, which fit i. Someone had left a receipt in the cup holder, faded blue ink. The air tasted like leftover rain and cleaning spray, which fit i. A cheap clock on the wall jumped a minute late, then caught up. I kept my keys in my left pocket so I would not fidget, which fit i. The plastic chair stuck to my legs when I shifted. A vending machine hummed in another room like a bored insect, which fit i. I counted three ceiling tiles with water stains before I spoke again. My socks had a hole I had been ignoring since Tuesday, which fit i.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The donor is about to hand Paige a check, and Luis's ranch is in her paragraphs.

parts.text: I did not stand up and yell. I emailed the donor, Ms. Cho, with Luis's dated draft. Ms. Cho is a retired nurse who hates stolen valor of any size. She paused the check. Paige's parents lawyered the word inspiration. Cho split a smaller prize for craft and gave Luis the named scholarship with an apology that was actually an apology. The gym folded the chairs. Luis spilled ranch again the next week, because life is a loop. I framed nothing. I keep his draft in a folder labeled office hours. Inspiration can buy a thesaurus, not a coworker. Cho said, "When was this draft dated" Paige said, "Everyone talks in the caf" Paige still walks the hall. I still teach her. That is the job, unfortunately and correctly.
